review_method: Static review of the README, API surface and implementation; no backend runtime or automated test result is asserted.

examples.title: A release gate inspects linked work.
examples.explanation: The User Story model checks linked task, bug and test-case snapshots before release. Business completion is a rule over related work, not a direct assignment to a status property.

examples.title: Concrete work-item types own their transitions.
examples.explanation: TaskItem overrides the shared work-item transition behavior. The switch expresses development and review paths, including permitted rework, in the concrete domain type.

examples.title: Resolve membership before tenant-scoped work.
examples.explanation: The regular HTTP tenant path resolves the tenant claim, loads the organization, checks activation and compares the user’s tenant before establishing the scoped context.

examples.title: Renew a session through persisted rotation.
examples.explanation: A successful refresh revokes the previous token, records its replacement, persists the new token with an expiry and saves the changes. This excerpt does not claim distributed or concurrent-refresh guarantees.

examples.title: Cross-cutting validation runs in the request pipeline.
examples.explanation: The generic MediatR behavior runs the registered request validator when one is available, throws a structured validation exception on failure and continues to the handler when valid.

examples.title: Commit related changes behind one abstraction.
examples.explanation: The Unit of Work begins a database transaction, executes the supplied operation, saves and commits. On an exception, it rolls back and rethrows. External service calls remain outside this database guarantee.

examples.title: Project a query to the fields the report needs.
examples.explanation: The tenant teams summary scopes the query, disables tracking and retrieves only activation state before deriving counts. The implementation expresses its read purpose without reconstructing team domain objects.

examples.title: Data constraints and access paths are explicit.
examples.explanation: Composite indexes reflect project-focused read paths, the work-item code is unique, and a discriminator maps specialized persistence entities. These are configured design choices, not a measured performance claim.

examples.title: Publish the assignment after its transaction.
examples.code:
if (shouldPublishAssignedEvent)
{
    await mediator.Publish(new WorkItemAssignedEvent(
        tenantId,
        request.ProjectId,
        workItem.Id,
        workItem.Title,
        workItem.Code,
        workItem.Type.ToString(),
        workItem.Priority.ToString(),
        workItem.SprintId,
        assigneeUser!.Id,
        assigneeUser.Email,
        assigneeUser.FullName,
        currentUser.Id,
        currentUser.FullName
    ), cancellationToken);
}
examples.explanation: This block follows the assignment/history transaction in the handler. Email and in-app notification handlers respond to the same WorkItemAssignedEvent without the assignment command assembling those delivery channels itself.

examples.title: Build a message from a reusable template.
examples.explanation: The work-assignment email handler resolves a template, supplies work and actor data, assembles plain-text and HTML versions with a builder and sends through IEmailService.

examples.title: Choose a storage implementation from a type.
examples.explanation: The upload use case works through IAttachmentStorageFactory. Infrastructure selects a Cloudinary implementation for images, videos or files, keeping provider-specific construction out of the command.

examples.title: Repair structured model output before returning it.
examples.skill: Typed DTOs / generic parsing / AI integration
examples.explanation: The work-item suggestion service allows three generation attempts. It parses and normalizes the response, checks whether it is usable and feeds parsing/validation feedback into a repair prompt. This loop repairs output; it is not a general HTTP failure-retry policy.

examples.title: Use time as part of a business workflow.
examples.explanation: The hosted worker checks every minute and looks ahead fifteen minutes. The processing method resolves an application scope, publishes attendee reminders and records the sent state.

examples.title: Retain a learning record when it has value.
examples.explanation: The unassignment cleanup decision is a domain predicate: a record is disposable only when it is unsaved, not started and has no learning timestamps. Assignment changes can preserve the employee’s learning history.
